sources.title: Review of the Safety of LHC Collisions

author: John Ellis
Gian Giudice
Michelangelo Mangano
Igor Tkachev
Urs Wiedemann
provenance.venue: Journal of Physics G: Nuclear and Particle Physics, vol. 35, no. 11

sources.conflict_of_interest: All five authors were employed by CERN at the time of writing. CERN has an institutional interest in LHC operations proceeding. The report was submitted to and published by an independent peer-reviewed journal.
sources.notes: Primary safety assessment known as the LSAG report. Commissioned by CERN in response to public concern prior to LHC start-up. Addresses four proposed hazard classes: micro black holes, strangelets, magnetic monopoles, and vacuum bubbles. Concluded by an independent review committee.

sources.title: Astrophysical implications of hypothetical stable TeV-scale black holes

author: Steven B. Giddings
Michelangelo Mangano
provenance.institution: University of California, Santa Barbara and CERN

sources.conflict_of_interest: Mangano is a CERN staff physicist. Giddings is an independent academic at UC Santa Barbara with no CERN employment; his inclusion reduces the institutional homogeneity concern.
sources.notes: The paper specifically addresses the scenario in which Hawking radiation does not occur, providing an astrophysical safety argument independent of any unverified theoretical mechanism. Peer-reviewed in Physical Review D.

sources.title: Study of Potentially Dangerous Events During Heavy-Ion Collisions at the LHC
sources.conflict_of_interest: Same author team as src_001. The 2003 and 2008 reports share the same five authors, making them correlated rather than fully independent institutional assessments.
sources.notes: The earlier safety report, produced in the context of preparation for LHC heavy-ion collisions. Its conclusions were later updated and extended in the LSAG 2008 report (src_001). The shared authorship with src_001 means the two reports should not be treated as fully independent confirmations.

sources.title: Search for microscopic black holes in pp collisions at sqrt(s) = 7 TeV

provenance.author: CMS Collaboration
provenance.venue: Journal of High Energy Physics, vol. 2012, no. 4

sources.conflict_of_interest: The CMS Collaboration is a large international scientific collaboration operating at CERN. No direct financial conflict of interest identified, though note the institutional context.
sources.notes: Representative CMS micro-BH search. Subsequent searches at 8 TeV and 13 TeV provided stronger constraints. Specific numerical limits in extracted claims should be verified against the published paper. The result is a null result constraining specific ADD model parameter configurations.

sources.title: A Large Mass Hierarchy from a Small Extra Dimension (ADD model)
sources.notes: The foundational ADD (Arkani-Hamed, Dimopoulos, Dvali) paper proposing large extra spatial dimensions as a solution to the hierarchy problem. This is the theoretical framework under which micro-BH production at LHC energies becomes conceivable. The model has not been empirically confirmed. The authors have no stake in the safety question.

sources.title: Black Hole Explosions?
sources.notes: The original theoretical paper predicting that black holes emit thermal radiation due to quantum effects near the event horizon. Widely accepted as a valid theoretical derivation in semi-classical gravity. As of the LSAG review (2008), the prediction had not been directly confirmed experimentally. Fundamental to the HR-based safety argument.

sources.title: Gravitational radiation from collider experiments with extra dimensions
sources.notes: Theoretical paper calculating black hole production cross-sections at colliders under extra-dimension models. One of the primary theoretical sources establishing the predicted rates and signatures of micro-BH production at LHC energies. Specific numerical claims require verification against the published paper.

sources.title: Complaint for Declaratory and Injunctive Relief (Wagner v. United States Department of Energy)

author: Walter L. Wagner
Luis Sancho
provenance.venue: United States District Court, District of Hawaii, Civil No. 08-00136

sources.conflict_of_interest: Wagner has previously filed similar legal challenges against other high-energy physics experiments including the RHIC. Neither plaintiff holds a physics PhD. The court dismissed the case on jurisdictional grounds without evaluating the scientific merits.
sources.notes: Legal challenge seeking an injunction to halt LHC operations. Dismissed on jurisdictional grounds in August 2008 because CERN is not a US entity. The scientific arguments in the complaint were not adjudicated on their merits. Included for completeness of the epistemic record; the complaint represents one formalization of the public risk concern.
